| DecodeBase64 | `src/equicordplugins/baseDecoder` | `plugins/chat/decodebase64` | Complete | A message's hover bar gets upstream's decode button: a left click shows the decoded text and a right click copies it, swapped when Click method is Right; its tooltip says which is which. Like upstream, every run of four or more Base64 characters (with optional = padding) is decoded, and the ones that make valid UTF-8 text are kept. Decode shows them in a "Decoded Base64 Content" window, each in a code box with Copy ("Decoded content copied to clipboard!"). A message with nothing to decode says "No Base64 content found in this message.". Qord also puts both actions in the message's right-click menu, the click method's left-click one first. On purpose, unlike upstream: copying puts all decoded parts on the clipboard, one per line (upstream copies each in turn, so only the last stays), and non-ASCII text is decoded as UTF-8 (upstream shows it byte by byte). |

| FakeNitro | `src/plugins/fakeNitro` | `plugins/chat/fakenitro` | Complete | Emojis and stickers you can't use are sent as links ([name](url) by default); messages that are only such a link show the emoji or sticker instead, and the link's image embed is hidden. Hovering a shown FakeNitro emoji or sticker says what it is, as upstream's popout notice does. Discord's own sticker packs (offered last in the sticker picker) are free and always sent as stickers. With the bypasses on, the emoji picker and autocomplete (for messages, not reactions) and the sticker picker offer every server's emojis and stickers. Animated (APNG) stickers are redrawn as a GIF and added to the message box, as upstream puts them in the upload queue; Qord's GIF writer keeps transparency by alpha where upstream's gifenc palette does not. An emoji kept to roles you don't have is sent as a link unless you administer its server; Qord can't tell role subscription roles from other roles, so this covers upstream's role subscription check and other role-locked emojis. The stream quality bypass makes Go Live offer every resolution up to 4K and 60 FPS, as with Nitro. Qord extras, not in upstream: long messages are split into several (code blocks closed and reopened across the cut, @silent kept on each part, each sent once the one before it was accepted, the rest dropped if one fails), the message box counts down the last 200 characters and, past the limit, says how many messages it will send; images over the upload limit are shrunk to fit, animated ones as a smaller GIF (frames scaled, then every other frame dropped), and videos are re-encoded to MP4 (H.264 and AAC) at a bitrate worked out from their length, a resolution and frame rate (at most 30) that bitrate can carry, keeping a phone video's rotation, all on a worker thread with a notice while it runs; emojis among other text can be sent smaller than ones on their own; and the link text can be hidden. The emoji link's base URL follows Discord's IconUtils.getEmojiURL as far as can be read from upstream (cdn.discordapp.com/emojis/<id>.webp?size=N, with animated=true for animated emojis); it cannot be checked against Discord's own code here. When an edit is cancelled at the embed permission prompt the edit is dropped, where Discord keeps the editor open. Received fake emojis are found with Qord's markdown link rules, outside code; with compound sentences on, links nested in formatting are transformed too, where upstream only transforms top-level ones. not applicable: Nitro client themes and app icons: Qord has its own themes and no Discord gradient client themes or app icons, which upstream unlocks and keeps from being overwritten by synced settings; Soundboard: Qord has no soundboard, so upstream's unlocking of all soundboard sounds has nothing to unlock. |
| FakeProfileThemes | `src/plugins/fakeProfileThemes` | `plugins/appearance/fakeprofilethemes` | Complete | Like upstream, a bio holding "[#rrggbb,#rrggbb]" as invisible Unicode tag characters (3y3) shows that profile with those theme colours: the popup in a gradient from the primary to the accent colour, the banner in the primary one when it has no image or colour of its own. With "Nitro colors" first, a profile's own Nitro theme wins. The settings page has upstream's colour pickers and "Copy 3y3", which copies the invisible text to paste into your bio; its preview is "Preview", which opens your profile with the picked colours for a minute. Qord itself now shows Nitro profile themes (theme_colors), which it didn't before, and leaves the tag characters out of shown bios, as Discord does. Upstream's "Copy 3y3" button in Discord's own profile editor has no counterpart: Qord has no profile editor, so the bio is edited in Discord. |

| Translate | `src/plugins/translate` | `plugins/utility/translate` | Complete | A message's hover bar has upstream's Translate button (and its right-click menu has Translate too); the translation is shown under it after the translate icon. "Translate" in a message's menu shows the translation under it ("translated from X - Dismiss"). The chat bar button opens the languages window (searchable lists for the received and sent languages, and Auto Translate); Shift+click or right-click toggles auto-translate, with upstream's notice the first time. With auto-translate on, a message waits in the locked message box until it is translated, with "Auto Translate Enabled" over the button for two seconds. Google needs no key; DeepL (free or pro, falling back to Google when the quota runs out) and Kagi take an API key or session token, which Qord keeps in the system keychain instead of the settings file. The settings page has upstream's "Customize translation languages & Auto-Translate" button, which opens the languages window, and shows the DeepL key only while DeepL is chosen and the Kagi session only while Kagi is. A message auto-translation fails on is sent as written, as upstream does. |

| UnitConverter | `src/equicordplugins/unitConverter` | `plugins/utility/unitconverter` | Complete | A message's hover bar has upstream's Convert Units button (it's also in the right-click menu); the converted text is shown under the message after the conversion icon. "Convert Units" in a message's right-click menu shows the message again under it with its units converted to the ones you use ("My units"), with Dismiss to remove it. Converting to imperial: Celsius, centimeters, meters (as feet and inches), kilometers, km/h, grams and kilograms; to metric: Fahrenheit, feet, inches, 5'11", 5 ft 11 in, pounds, 5 lb 3 oz, ounces and mph. Upstream's arithmetic slips are fixed: inches are multiplied by 2.54 (upstream divides), meters use 3.281 feet (upstream 3.821), "5 lb 3 oz" counts the ounces, 1.75 m reads 5ft8.88in rather than rounding the feet up, and "50 km/h" converts as a speed instead of as "50 km" followed by "/h"; and a number and unit inside a word, such as the "8g" of a Base64 string or the "5 g" of "5 great", are left alone. |
